title: The joint fabric: rock breaks along its own grain
question: Does this read as the craquelure you asked for - and is the density right, or still too much?
context_md:
You asked three times for the Voronoi pattern from your worldgen image. This is it. Rock now has a latent **grain** everywhere - a Worley cell structure - and a blast reveals the joints near it instead of drawing a star across the stone. An edge is a joint when its two cells belong to different cells of that grain, which is a zero-width closed curve, so the polygons are sealed by construction and the edges are straight because Voronoi boundaries are straight. The scribble is gone structurally, not tuned away.

**Scrub the sequence.** It is one buried charge, every 4th frame. The bang is at frame 60: the rock is intact at 59 and the seam web is already open at 63. That is the other half of your last verdict - breakage used to arrive 7 to 15 seconds late because it waited on a structural wavefront. Seams now open at detonation. The GIF of the same run is in the chat if you want to feel the pace.

**Two things I did deliberately against the reference.**

You said of that worldgen image *"the voronoi pattern is too much. I like a little of it, but there is too much."* So this ships sparser than it, on purpose, and the number agrees: total cracked cells in the world went **down** 45%, 6,185 to 3,368, against the build you just rejected. Less ink, more structure. And the seams near the crater are **opened** into real voids with grit in them - your reference's black lines are carved void, not darkened rock, which is why nothing I drew could ever look like it.

**The honest cost, and the thing to tell me if it bothers you:** a charge now eats about twice the rock - 4,136 cells to 8,472 on the worst seed. That is the price of opening seams. `joint_open_fraction` is the lever and it is already turned down from 0.45 to 0.30; say the word and it goes lower.

Already measured, don't spend attention on it: nothing moves in sand or in air (zero joints), the chisel and strike paths are bit-identical, and the frame cost went *down* (59.9ms to 49.2ms worst frame). Ignore the trees.

items.label: one buried charge, every 4th frame
items.caption: bang at frame 60; intact at 59, seams open at 63
